title.narrative: Provision of life-saving food assistance to conflict- affected households in Lower Juba (Kismayo and Afmadow District).

description.narrative: In light of recent clashes between Jubaland forces and Al-Shabaab in key areas of Lower Jubba, particularly Kismayo, Afmadow, and Dhobley, the conflict has led to significant civilian displacement, heightening the need for food assistance and protection services. The deteriorating security and large-scale displacement underscore the need for urgent, coordinated humanitarian action to mitigate the impact on affected communities. Swift and comprehensive responses from regional and international actors are critical to addressing this escalating crisis. WFP, through CERF funding, will provide emergency relief assistance to meet essential food needs through cash-based transfers to 22,488 people over the next three months. Each household will receive USD 180 over the course of 3 months with each household receiving an average of USD 60 per month. This intervention will leverage the overall humanitarian operation coverage in Kismayo and Afmadow ensuring efficient and timely delivery of relief assistance. This will be facilitated through a coordinated efforts with local authorities, the Food Security Cluster, and partners will minimize duplication and enhance a multi-sectoral approach, while complementing other ongoing and planned humanitarian efforts in the region.
